newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL TIN HITS 5-1/2 MONTH HIGH ON WEAK RINGGIT.
newsitem.headline: KL TIN HITS 5-1/2 MONTH HIGH ON WEAK RINGGIT.

text.p: Malaysia's tin price rose 18 cents a kg to a new 5-1/2-month high of 14.70 ringgit ($5.42) per kg on Monday as the Malaysian currency continued to weaken against the U.S. dollar, traders said.
The metal's last highest spot-price in Kuala Lumpur was 14.72 ringgit, notched on February 20.
The ringgit fell to a 42-month low against the dollar in late morning trading on Monday on continued sales by offshore and local players, dealers said.
At 1240 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.7280/7300 to a dollar, its lowest level since March 28, 1994.
"It's the main factor for the rise of the (tin) price this morning," said a trader. "There were lots of buyers coming in despite the fall of the LME (London Metal Exchange) on Friday)."
He set the market's immediate resistance at 14.75 ringgit if profit-taking did not set in and the ringgit stayed weak.
"It all depends on how the ringgit performs now," he added.
Traders said the price on the Kuala Lumpur market was now at par with the LME, after trading at a premium of $5 on Friday.
At the opening, there were initial bids for 335 tonnes against sales offers for 127 tonnes.
Final turnover was 179 tonnes, against the 217 on Friday, and was absorbed by Japanese, European and local interests.
